method: Transparent independent hand derivations; separate executed records exist for the numerical API examples.

derivations.probability: Four equally likely cards: P(cat)=3/4=.75; P(dog)=1/4=.25; the disjoint exhaustive outcomes sum to4/4=1. Two probabilities .9+.9=1.8 cannot be an exhaustive disjoint cat/dog distribution.
derivations.negative_log: For p=e^a with p>0, log(p)=a. On 0<p≤1, -log(p)≥0 and d[-log(p)]/dp=-1/p<0. At p=1 it is0; as p→0+ it diverges. Independence permits P(both)=.5*.5=.25; -ln(.25)=2*(-ln(.5))=1.3862943611, displayed1.386. Values0.9,0.5,0.1 yield0.1053605157,0.6931471806,2.3025850930 respectively.
derivations.W3_means: Row sums210 and270 divided by3 give70 and90. Column sums140,160,180 divided by2 give70,80,90. Replacing scores[0,2]=80 with110 raises the first row mean by30/3=10 and the third column mean by30/2=15; results[80,90] and[70,80,105]. Shape[2,4,3] at index0 retains the4×3 axes; six entries reshape to6 and back2×3, not8.
derivations.W5_products: [2,1,0] dot [10,20,30]=40; dot[0,1,4]=1. [1,2,1] dot costs=80 and sweetness=6. Adding bias[5,0] yields[45,1],[85,6]; bias[8,0] yields[48,1],[88,6]. Matrix indices C_ij=Σ_k recipes_ik weights_kj sum only the matching material axis; student/shop axis i remains independent.
derivations.W6_derivative: For L(w)=(w-3)^2, [L(w+h)-L(w)]/h=2(w-3)+h for h≠0, so limit h→0 is2(w-3). Atw=1 derivative=-4; at1.4 derivative=-3.2. L(1)=4 andL(1.1)=3.61, change=-.39.
derivations.W6_steps: One stepw_new=1-lr*(-4)=1+4lr. lr=.1 gives1.4,L=2.56; lr=.6 gives3.4,L=.16; lr=1.1 gives5.4,L=5.76. In this quadratic, L_new=4(1-2lr)^2. Relative toL_old=4, a positive learning rate improves iff0<lr<1; the example explicitly refrains from claiming a universal step-size guarantee.

empirical_scope: The page makes no measured model-quality, speedup, generalization or formal training-result claim. The hand-set Linear weights and one scalar parameter update are mechanism examples, not trained model capability evidence.
